documentNotes.title: Read once more before you start your work
documentNotes.statement:
**Languages of the solutions.** (For Practical and also for Observational rounds).

No text in any language is permitted to use in solutions. All the solution must be written using only drawing pictures, plotting graph, writing formulae, numerical values and standard international astronomy symbols (like ♂, ♎, α UMa, M31, 5ᵐ). Numerical values must be written using standard symbols but not symbols of National alphabet. Jury of the Practical round will not take into account any text in any language in solution.

For example, the names of constellations, written in English, Russian or any other language will be not taken into account (should be only UMa, Ori, etc.).

paper.caveat: The official key supplies numerical answers and plotting instructions but no completed transit/scatter/radial plots; none have been invented. Its D notation is used both for a magnitude depth and a squared radius ratio, retained with a source note. The complete two-page solution PDF also contains the separate alpha problem7, read for boundary context but not applied to beta. The archive contains only practalphasol.xlsx, no matching beta workbook. The data.pdf constants and hrd.pdf diagram are explicitly labelled Round Theo. Both were inspected as archive references; their provision during the practical round is not asserted. The H–R diagram is unrelated to these two beta tasks and is not reproduced as a problem figure.

problems.title: Transiting extra-solar planet.
problems.statement: The transit of an extra-solar planet (TrES-3b) across a star (TrES-3) was observed by the 1-m telescope of Weihai Observatory (WHO) on April 16, 2009, using the broad-band V filter and a PI CCD. The photometric data (selected part from the original one) are given in the Table 6 (see separate sheet), the time is in Julian days, and $m_V$ is the V-band magnitude.

parts.statement: Plot the transit light curve (magnitude vs time), determine the moment of mid-transit (the deepest transit) and write result (in Julian days) in form of «$T_{\mathrm{mid}}=\ldots$», estimate the duration of the transit (in days) in form of «$T_d=\ldots$», determine the depth of the transit (in magnitudes) in form of «$D=\ldots$».

answer.value: Tmid = …8.272 JD; Td = 0.055 days; D = 0.027 mag (as printed).

parts.statement: Give the formula and calculate the radius of the extra-solar planet TrES-3b $R_p$ (in units of the radius of Jupiter: $R_{\mathrm{Jupiter}}$, write the answer in form of «$R_p=\ldots$»). The radius of the star (TrES-3) is known to be 0.813 radius of the Sun, $R_s=0.813R_{\mathrm{sun}}$.

Estimate the approximate value of the angle $i$, in unit of degrees (°) between the axis of this planet’s orbiting and the line of sight of the observer. Write the answer in form of «$i\approx\ldots$».

The next mid-transit moment after the above transit event was: JD = 2454939.578. The mass of the star (TrES-3) is known to be 0.924 mass of the Sun, $M_s=0.924M_{\mathrm{sun}}$. Calculate the orbital period of TrES-3b (in units of days, in form of «$P=\ldots$»), and the semi-major axis of the orbit (in units of au, in form of «$a=\ldots$»).

sections.statement:
Plot the transit light curve properly, should care about the scales, and the magnitudes axis (y-axis) should be reversed (i.e. from high values to low values).

$$T_{\mathrm{mid}}=\ldots8.272\ \mathrm{JD};\quad T_d=0.055\ \mathrm{days};\quad D=0.027^{\mathrm m}.$$

(some errors in above values accepted)

$$D=(R_p/R_s)^2\quad\text{(or other similar ones)};$$

$$R_p=1.305R_J\quad\text{(some errors accepted)}.$$

Source note: the key prints the same symbol $D$ here as for the magnitude depth in 6.1; the notation is retained without silently converting its definition.

$$P=1.3062\ \mathrm{days};\qquad a=0.0226\ \mathrm{au}.$$

(some errors in above values accepted)

problems.title: Spectral observation on an interacting galaxy.
problems.statement: The low-resolution spectra of 15 different regions in an interacting galaxy **Arp 86** were observed by Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS) on the 2.16-m telescope of Xinglong Station near Beijing, National Astronomical Observatories of China. The data is analyzed by Zhou et al. (2014, RAA, 14, 1393). The measured fluxes of the [OIII], Hβ, [NII], Hα emission lines are shown in Table β7 (see separate sheet). The fluxes are in units of $10^{-16}\ \mathrm{erg/s/cm^2}$.

parts.statement: Plot the scatter diagram between $\log_{10}(\mathrm{[OIII]}/\mathrm{H}\beta)$ vs. $\log_{10}(\mathrm{[NII]}/\mathrm{H}\alpha)$ for regions in the galaxy.

Draw a dashed curve on the diagram for the diagnostic function:

$$\log_{10}(\mathrm{[OIII]}/\mathrm{H}\beta)=1.3+\frac{0.61}{\log_{10}(\mathrm{[NII]}/\mathrm{H}\alpha)-0.05},$$

given by Kauffmann et al. (2003, MNRAS, 346, 1055). If the point of a region in the diagram is above this curve, the region can be classified as “AGN” (Active Galactic Nuclei). Determine which regions can be classified as “AGN”, write the answer in form of «AGN = “Region ID” …». (“Region ID” are given in the 1st column of Table β7.)

In your answer book draw a table in form of the following example. Calculate the angular distance between each region to the center ($\alpha=23^h47^m04.8^s$, $\delta=+29^\circ29'00.6''$) of the galaxy (in units of arcsec). Calculate the luminosities of Hα ($L(\mathrm{H}\alpha)$) for each region (in units of erg/s), and then estimate the Star Formation Rate (SFR) for each region based on Hα luminosities, following the formula:

$$\mathrm{SFR}\ (M_\odot/\mathrm{yr})=7.9\times10^{-42}[L(\mathrm{H}\alpha)]\ (\mathrm{erg/s}).$$

Calculate the metallicities (oxygen abundance in units of $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$) of interstellar medium (ISM) for each region, following the formula:

$$12+\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})=8.9+0.57\times\log_{10}(\mathrm{[NII]}/\mathrm{H}\alpha).$$

The redshift of **Arp 86** is: 0.016.

| Region ID | Angular Distance to the center (arcsec) | $L(\mathrm{H}\alpha)$ (erg/s) | SFR ($M_\odot$/yr) | $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | | | | |
| 2 | | | | |

Plot the radial distribution of the $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$ of this galaxy. The radial distribution should be plotted as a scatter diagram: $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$ vs. $\beta$, where $\beta$ is angular distance to the center in arcsec.

Draw a straight dashed line on the scatter diagram of oxygen abundance ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$) radial distribution to indicate the trend of the profile. If there is a linear relation between $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})$ and $\beta$, i.e. $\log_{10}(\mathrm{O/H})=A+B\times\beta$, estimate $B$ with help of graphical method, write the answer in form of «$B=\ldots$».
